title: Ang 1086–1094: Maru ki Var M3
tomorrow: what did Bebe whisper before every hard day?

cards: A show's new episode starts with a fast recap: previously on. A few quick cuts, and the whole season is back in your head. Here's this week of Maru, in one breath.
A coin with real silver, whatever's scrawled on the paper. Two houses awake at night, and ease for the one free of both. Sixteen stanzas, the sound and the sense.
The dark before the world, already full. Which way you're facing. And a humble walk that answers mockery with peace.
Six days. One raga of courage.

teach.b: Today's pages turn that kind of recap into a form. From ang 1086 comes Maru ki Var, a ballad by Guru Amar Das, the third Guru.
A var climbs in pauris, stanzas like steps, with short saloks set before them. Ballads were the songs people sang about heroes. Here the hero is the Guru's Word, and the battle is inside.
One salok puts it plainly, in paraphrase: without the Guru, the illness doesn't break, and the pain of ego doesn't leave.
That's the week, folded into one line. The ego was the counterfeit print on the paper. It was the worry in both houses.
It was the mind turned to stare at itself. And the steady thing, every day, was a turning: toward the silver, toward the Guru, toward peace.
A ballad repeats on purpose, coming back to its refrain. So did this week.

how: Guru Amar Das's Maru ki Var is sung in kirtan pauri by pauri, each with its saloks, and read in order in a complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib.

s: a var in the Granth is a song about soldiers in a real battle
Maru ki Var keeps the ballad's steps, but the battle it sings about is inside: ego.
one salok here says, in effect, that without the Guru the pain of ego doesn't leave
the illness of ego is the thread running through the week.
this week's Maru hymns all say courage means being loud
quiet courage: trusting the silver, turning to face the Guru, answering with peace.

games.q: your younger brother wins a big game and won't stop bragging. by this week's Maru, what's the gentlest true thing to tell him?
o: great game; just don't let the win run the night, like plenty can.
real winners never feel proud, so stop feeling it.
you'll lose next time anyway, so it doesn't matter.
games.why: the house with plenty worries too; ego is the illness Maru ki Var names. joy is fine; being ruled by it is the trap.

practice: Take a pen and a scrap of paper, and write one line from this week by hand, slowly, the one that stuck. Brave faith; free of both; before the beginning; which way am I facing; peace.
Then sit with the page in front of you and read it once more, silently.
